jobs.title: Global Public Policy Manager, Compute, Infrastructure & Sovereign AI

reading.body:
Two open AI policy and governance roles are listed, one at a consultancy in Munich and one at Cohere covering compute, infrastructure, and sovereign AI.

The sample is too small to describe a hiring trend. What it does show is the shape of the work: one role sits inside a professional services firm selling governance advice, the other sits inside a model developer and names compute and infrastructure directly in its title. Policy work in AI is not only about rules. It is also about where the machines go and who supplies the power for them.

That second title is the only place in this data where compute, infrastructure, and sovereign AI appear together, and it appears as a job function rather than a buildout figure. Nothing here reports capacity, electricity, or construction. The two postings carry dates in September and October 2026, and the page was generated on 6 October 2026, so the window is narrow and the count is two.

The listed sources include federal, aggregated, remote, and European job boards plus company career pages, so the pool the page draws from is broad. Whether that pool was searched exhaustively for this function is not stated. Read the two roles as examples of how AI policy work is being staffed, not as a measure of how much of it exists.
